extracted.intended_audience: writers querying literary agents / authors seeking representation
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and a checklist of submission 'no-no's' for writers preparing query letters, sample pages, and other initial materials to send to literary agents. Focuses on etiquette, formatting, content, and common mistakes that turn agents off.

rubrics_metrics.name: No typos or similar errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Typos and other similar errors in your query and manuscript are a sign of a writer who isn't giving his work enough attention and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such mistakes signal unprofessionalism; agents seek professionalism. Proofread, edit, and have others read your work before querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor each query to a specific agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each query should be tailored and individualized for a specific agent—you are querying a specific agent at that agency, not the agency as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the agent by name rather than 'Dear [Agency] agents.' Show you've done agent-specific research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid negativity in your query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid negativity in a query letter—in all forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not complain about past rejections, industry frustrations, or express bitterness—agents are turned off by negativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paste initial unsolicited material into the email body
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all agents want text pasted into the e-mail body for initial unsolicited submissions (query text, synopsis, and sample pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments are rarely requested for initial queries—use pasted text unless the agent explicitly asks for attachments. Agents tolerate some wonky formatting to avoid attachments (viruses). Once material is solicited, attachments (Word/PDF) are fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow stated agent submission preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent clearly states what genres they like and what submission guidelines they request, listen and follow those instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring explicit guidance is insulting and unlikely to be effective—adhere to posted preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't be rude or unkind about other people
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't bestow compliments on an agent while speaking unkindly of others in the industry; bitterness shows up in queries and turns agents off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professionalism and civility when referring to people or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't make demands or sound impatient
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers who send unsolicited submissions are in no position to make demands; avoid language that makes you sound impatient or annoyed with the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lines like 'Thank you for your prompt response' which can read as passive-aggressive. Do not request or demand rapid replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't respond negatively to a rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent rejects your book, do not send any kind of negative response (e.g., begging, whining, pleading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative/unprofessional responses can blacklist you from that agent and their agency; keep responses professional and brief if you reply at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only submit the types of work agents represent
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary agents represent completed books; they generally do not represent film/TV, stage plays, poetry, magazine articles, or single short stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send book-length projects to literary agents; seek specialist agents for scripts or other formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: If represented, sever ties properly before querying another agent
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an existing agent, completely sever ties formally (per contract terms) before seeking new representation; do not secretly query while still represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow contract language for termination (often a waiting period). Provide your new agent with submission history from prior representation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use email for submissions except during pitch events
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it's the day of a specific pitch party (#PitMad, #DVpit), follow submission guidelines and send your work via e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch parties may have special protocols; otherwise, email is standard for queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks are useful but don't substitute for a proper query
rubrics_metrics.description: You can hyperlink claims in your query (e.g., publications, clips), but don't send only a link with little or no query text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantive query content; hyperlinks are supporting material, not a replacement for a clear pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain briefly why you picked that agent (but be specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to explain why you've picked that agent with a specific, genuine line rather than a generic statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good: cite a specific tweet or interest; Bad: 'Because you represent romance' or generic statements that add no value—omit a forced connection if you can't make it unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use professional salutations; avoid pet names
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional. Don't use words like honey, darling, sweetie, or babe in your salutation or query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agent's name and professional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't ask agents for referrals to other agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask agents to refer you to other agents who might be interested—research agents yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency hides their genre list, it's a sign they don't want cold submissions—better not to query them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exclamation points
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclamation points are almost never a good idea in queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for energetic genres, avoid excessive punctuation that reads as unprofessional or breathless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize your salutation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize salutations and submissions—don't send generic, mass queries with impersonal greetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address agents by name and include details that reflect genuine research (without being clumsy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid opening/closing with rhetorical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting or ending your query pitch with a rhetorical question is overused and ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a strong declarative hook or concise pitch instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear about era/setting for historical fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: For historical fiction, be upfront about the era—you should not hide the specific time period of your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the era concisely so an agent immediately understands the setting and market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query only one agent per agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard protocol is to only query one agent at an agency; a 'no' from that agent is typically a 'no' from the entire agency for that project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Querying multiple agents at the same agency can be discovered and will not impress them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of politically sensitive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents tend to be educated and politically correct; avoid using outdated or offensive terms in the query (e.g., 'mulatto', 'handicapped', slurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character uses problematic language, be cautious including it in the query; aim for sensitivity in your pitch. In the manuscript, flawed character speech can be appropriate if handled intentionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-praise and grandiose adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Any self-praise for your own work is almost never advised—don't call your own work 'enthralling' or 'brilliant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention objective credentials like awards instead of subjective superlatives about your own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rely on gimmicks
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist gimmicks (singing a pitch in person, writing a query from the main character's perspective, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gimmicks signal weakness; if the story and writing are strong, you don't need unusual approaches. Avoid attempts at novelty that distract from the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard manuscript fonts and normal formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard manuscript fonts include Cambria, Times New Roman, or Arial. Avoid odd fonts and strange formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stick to industry-standard formatting; do not do anything weird or strange with font or layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be patient with your work; revise before querying
rubrics_metrics.description: Impatience is a major impediment—don't rush to send out work when it still needs revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit, seek critique, go through drafts, and avoid submitting an early/incomplete draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't mention copyright registration in your query
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentioning that your work is copyrighted or registered is amateurish and can imply you think the agent might steal your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that your work is copyrighted when written; formal registration is unnecessary to mention in a query and can feel insulting to agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the writing speak for itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid over-explaining or over-selling—let the quality of the writing and the pitch do the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, concise pitch and strong sample pages rather than excessive promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not query in ways agents dislike even if you don't know preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent doesn't indicate whether they want attachments or pasted text, default to pasting into the email body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, follow the safer convention (paste) to respect agents' stated virus-avoidance preferences.
